results.name: cube with corners cut at 1/3 (truncated-cube type)

checks: M1 Omega_cube(0) = 64 for the cube [-1/2,1/2]^3 (known value)
M2 cube: vertex formula = product formula prod 1/((1/2 - x_i)(1/2 + x_i)) exactly at an interior point
M3 products: Omega_PxQ = Omega_P Omega_Q exactly at 14 random points (2D x 2D, 3D x 1D, 4D x 1D)
M4 every solid built with exact facets
M5 c_0 = 0 exactly at every direction (complete-fan identity)
M6 Omega(x0) = d! vol((P - x0)°) at an interior point (float polar hull, 1e-9) for 41 rational solids
M7 exact Omega(10^6 u) agrees with the series c_0..c_K to relative 1e-12 for 41 rational solids
M8 e is the same at all 3 directions for every solid
T3 zonotopes (15): c_k = 0 for k < d and c_d = the explicit formula, exactly, at every direction
T3 zonotopes: e = d (decay r^-2d) for every zonotope
T2 centrally symmetric solids (25): c_k = 0 whenever d + k is odd (k <= K)
T5 3D trichotomy (28 solids): e = 1 / 2 / 3 exactly as the facet predicate says (pairing; all faces centrally symmetric)
T5 3D: decay orders only r^-4, r^-5, r^-6
T4 local: w c_1 -> 0 at every facet hyperplane when e >= 2, w^2 c_2 -> 0 when e = 3 (171 facet lines, eps 1e-12)
T4 local NEGATIVE: for e = 2 solids some facet line has a true double pole of c_2 (w^2 c_2 not -> 0)
T6 products (8): e(P x Q) = e(P) + e(Q)
T7 Minkowski lineality bound (3): e >= r

H brief hypothesis "centrally symmetric => r^-(d+2)" REFUTED in 3D: centrally symmetric non-zonotopes decay like r^-4 (e = 1): octahedron, cuboctahedron, icosahedron, dodecahedron, cube with corners cut at 1/3 (truncated-cube type), rhombicuboctahedron
H brief hypothesis "all 2-faces symmetric => r^-(d+3)" REFUTED in 4D: zonotopes decay like r^-8 = r^-2d, not r^-7

C conjecture e(P) <= d with equality only for zonotopes: holds on every non-zonotope tested in 4D/5D (4-simplex e=1, 16-cell e=2, 24-cell e=2, triangle x square e=3, triangle x triangle e=2, tetrahedron x segment e=2, octahedron x segment e=2, TRD x segment e=3, triangle + generic 4-zonotope e=3, 5-simplex e=1, 5-cross-polytope e=1, triangle x triangle x segment e=3)
